sources.title: Introducing Amazon Nova foundation models: Frontier intelligence and industry leading price performance
sources.evidence: Dated December 3, 2024; introduces Nova Micro and says Nova models are available in Bedrock that day. Micro is a text-only 128K model optimized for low latency and cost, including summarization, translation, classification and interactive chat.

sources.title: What is Amazon Nova? (Version 1)
sources.evidence: Version 1 specification table maps Amazon Nova Micro to amazon.nova-micro-v1:0: text input/output, 128K context and Document Support = No. Lists interactive chat, RAG and agentic applications.

sources.title: Nova Micro - Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: Exact amazon.nova-micro-v1:0 model card confirms Amazon developer, text-only inputs/output, 128K context and client-side tool calling. Lists a conflicting Dec 05, 2024 launch date; the earlier dated launch announcement explicitly establishes public availability on Dec 3.

sources.title: The Amazon Nova Family of Models: Technical Report and Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened on October 27. Section 1.1 (PDF page 3) identifies the Transformer architecture and pretraining followed by SFT, reward modeling and preference optimization for Pro, Lite and Micro. It names no size-disclosed parent model and supplies no nominal total or active parameter count; the full PDF was downloaded and text-extracted after the web fetch exceeded its size limit.

sources.title: Amazon Nova Premier: Technical Report and Model Card
sources.evidence: April 30, 2025 addendum mentions distillation into Nova Micro but provides no Micro parameter-count or detailed architecture disclosure. Benchmark comparisons do not establish model size.

sources.title: Amazon Nova 2: Multimodal Reasoning and Generation Models
sources.evidence: December 2, 2025 later technical report checked for retrospective Micro specifications; the extracted report has no Micro or parameter-count entries. It does not resolve Micro size or dense/MoE structure.

sources.title: AWS AI Service Cards - Amazon Nova Micro, Lite, Pro, and Premier
sources.evidence: Service card current as of April 30, 2025 identifies Micro as text-input/text-output and describes Nova token inference as Transformer-based. It supplies no parameter counts or detailed Micro routing architecture.

sources.title: Iterative Training - Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Explicitly states that Amazon Nova weights are proprietary and customized checkpoints remain in escrow S3 buckets in AWS-managed accounts rather than being copied to customer accounts.

sources.title: Available foundation models - Amazon SageMaker AI
sources.evidence: Nova Micro / nova-textgeneration-micro row lists AWS Service Terms as its license. Although it appears in the broadly named Open-Weight Models table, explicit proprietary-weight and escrow documentation provides the more specific accessibility evidence.

sources.title: Complete request schema - Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: The inferenceConfig documentation restricts reasoningConfig to Nova Pro and Nova Lite, excluding Micro. Supports toolConfig and toolChoice; explicitly excludes image and video input for Micro.

sources.title: MASSIVE-Agents: A Benchmark for Multilingual Function-Calling in 52 Languages
sources.evidence: November 2025 Amazon AGI-authored comparison. Table 1 on PDF page 6 lists Nova Micro with Params = NP, alongside 128k context and December 2024 release. It has no activated-parameter column or count. This is explicit later first-party evidence that a nominal size is not supplied, rather than an inference from performance tier.

sources.title: PHLoRA: data-free Post-hoc Low-Rank Adapter extraction from full-rank checkpoint (workshop version)
sources.publisher: Amazon AGI and EdgeRunner AI / Amazon Science
sources.evidence: Sections 3.3 and 4 and Tables 3-4 evaluate Nova Micro using adapter ranks 32, 64 and 512. These are low-rank update dimensions, not model parameter counts. Nova Micro itself is the base for the custom fine-tunes; no total, active count or size-disclosed ancestor is identified. The assets.amazon.science URL returned 404; the same PDF was retrieved from cdn.amazon.science and text-extracted.

sources.title: PHLoRA: Data-Free Post-Hoc Low-Rank Adapter Extraction from Full-Rank Checkpoint (December 2025 archival version)
sources.publisher: Amazon AGI and EdgeRunner AI / ACL Anthology
sources.evidence: December 20-24, 2025 archival paper checked independently. Sections 4.1-4.3, Tables 3-4 and Appendix A.3 retain Nova Micro base/full-rank/adapter comparisons and rank hyperparameters, with no nominal total or active parameter count. Its base-model language describes custom fine-tuning of Nova Micro, not lineage from a separately sized base.

sources.title: Fine-tune Nova 1.0 - Amazon Nova
sources.evidence: Current full-rank and LoRA configuration table maps amazon.nova-micro-v1:0:128k to the base path nova-micro/prod. It discloses training settings and replica counts but no model size or alternate named base with a published size; neither adapter settings nor hardware replicas establish parameters.

name.note: Nova Micro is the official name; the existing 1.0 suffix identifies the documented Version 1 / v1 endpoint.

developer.note: First-party model announcement and Bedrock card identify Amazon.

family.note: Normalize to the documented Amazon Nova family; Micro is the model tier.

release_date.note: Earliest explicit public availability is the December 3 launch post. Current Bedrock card says December 5 without explaining the discrepancy; retain that conflict in notes rather than replacing launch evidence with lifecycle metadata.

open_weights.note: Explicit proprietary-weight escrow documentation outweighs the broad SageMaker table heading; no public weight release is established.

license.note: The exact Nova Micro row identifies AWS Service Terms; this is proprietary hosted-service access, not an open-weight license.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 search and reopened original/Premier/Nova 2 reports reveal no nominal total. Amazon AGI MASSIVE-Agents Table 1 explicitly gives Nova Micro Params = NP. Both later PHLoRA versions disclose adapter ranks only; original training and current customization documentation establish no size-disclosed named-base lineage. Tier, latency, hardware and adapter rank are not used to infer size.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh search for active/activated parameters and later first-party comparison tables found no separately reported active count. MASSIVE-Agents has only Params = NP for Micro; PHLoRA reports adapter ranks and task results, not per-token activated parameters. Dense versus MoE remains undisclosed, and no total-to-active equality is assumed.

architecture.note: Transformer backbone is explicit; dense versus mixture-of-experts structure and layer dimensions remain undisclosed.

context_window.note: AWS specifies 128K for amazon.nova-micro-v1:0; stored using the catalog decimal K convention.

modalities.note: The exact v1 table says text input/output and no document support. Text extracted from documents is ordinary text input, not native document support.

reasoning.note: Interpreted as dedicated configurable thinking/reasoning mode. Micro is excluded from reasoningConfig; ordinary mathematical reasoning or chain-of-thought prompting does not make this flag true.

tool_call.note: Exact Bedrock card explicitly supports client-side tool calling; request schema defines toolConfig/toolChoice.

description.value: Text-only Nova model for summarization, translation and classification, with a 128K-token context and tool calling.
description.note: Concrete documented text tasks, context and tool support without latency claims.

patch.notes: The Dec 3, 2024 launch announcement explicitly states availability; the current Bedrock card instead lists Dec 5, 2024, an unexplained date conflict. Transformer backbone is documented; total and active parameters remain undisclosed. Amazon AGI’s MASSIVE-Agents table lists Micro parameters as NP; PHLoRA reports adapter ranks only. No size-disclosed base lineage is established. Nova weights are proprietary and trained checkpoints remain in AWS-managed escrow. Micro accepts text only, with no native document input or configurable thinking mode. Endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit retains undisclosed total and active counts. Reopened original and later Nova reports; Amazon AGI MASSIVE-Agents explicitly lists Params = NP, while both PHLoRA versions and current customization documentation provide no nominal count or size-disclosed base lineage. Explicitly patch both counts and parameters_source to null. Preserve prior nonparameter assessments and corrections, including the Dec 3 launch and Dec 5 model-card discrepancy.
